title: from finished proof to the first *$600*
dek: The Jen work is not missing. It is over-separated. This brief reconnects the strongest visual demonstration, the deliverable that is ready now, the offer that can be sold honestly, and the proof events that still have to happen.
sources: 4 offer lanes + 2 client systems + proof ledger

sections.heading: the work is built; the commercial story is *fragmented*
sections.body:
Claude Design produced a strong presentation surface: First Home Valley is coherent, visually polished, and backed by a real content and lead-engine build. Codex should not redraw it. Codex's advantage is recovering the scattered decisions, keeping the proof labels honest, and turning the assets into a sequence that can produce a buyer event.

The immediate offer is the Listing Launch Kit, not the unfinished four-module Revenue Desk. The smallest truthful target is three founding kits at $200 each: $600 collected, three live delivery cycles, and a proof bank that can justify the $450 standard price. Jen's First Home Valley system remains the service-to-her and demonstration layer; her team becomes the warm validation channel only after she gives permission.

items.title: Jen's listing-content engine
items.body: A client-specific system for SFV listings: voice rules, verified property facts, shoot sheets, teleprompter scripts, captions, story sequences, DM keywords, and fair-housing checks. Willis, Armida, Moonseed, and Bothwell became the working examples.

items.title: Productization fork
items.body: The work branched into a low-ticket content subscription, a $950 Listing Launch Install, and a $750 four-module Revenue Desk. Red-team work killed the agency-first and generic-template logic. The Revenue Desk remained incomplete because Local Authority was partial and Lead Reactivation had not been built or tested.

items.title: Jen-Team Pilot
items.body: The broad product collapsed into a ready wedge: one active listing becomes a 48-hour Listing Launch Kit. Three founding spots at $200, a fictional sample, agent intake, pitch-day messages, visual carousels, and a proof ledger were completed.

items.title: First Home Valley
items.body: A separate service-to-Jen demonstration was completed: 12 designed assets, a buyer-objection demo, teleprompter flow, DM machine, math-sheet magnet, sourced flagship script, and launch plan. It is waiting on Jen's first-post pick, voice verdict, and channel greenlight.

items.title: Reconnect service, offer, and proof
items.body: First Home Valley earns the conversation with Jen. Her permission unlocks the three-agent Kit test. Paid use of the Kit earns the right to revisit the larger Revenue Desk.

sections.heading: run one *two-part* demonstration
sections.dek: Jen should see both the thing that serves her and the small offer that can serve agents she trusts. Do not ask the demo to sell four offers.

items.action: Show Jen First Home Valley as the service-to-her.
items.why: This keeps the emotional center correct: you are helping her build a buyer-education and conversation engine, not using her as a lead list. Capture her first-post pick, voice verdict, and channel greenlight.

items.action: Ask for permission to show one listing package to three agents.
items.why: Permission is the first missing proof event. Her yes unlocks the warm channel without implying endorsement, results, or an obligation to sell for you.

items.action: Offer three founding Listing Launch Kits at $200 each.
items.why: The deliverable exists, the scope is bounded, and three sales equal $600. Keep payment, delivery, use, conversations, repeat purchase, and referrals as separate receipts.

items.action: Earn the right to sell the $750 install later.
items.why: After one or more agents pay and use the flagship, the missing Lead Reactivation module can be built from real inputs. Until then, the Revenue Desk stays a parked expansion—not the front-door offer.

plays.title: Prepare the room
plays.intent: Open the First Home Valley review sheet and the sample Listing Launch Kit side by side so the demonstration moves from her business to the agent offer in under seven minutes.
plays.command: Open the First Home Valley demo, the visual review sheet, and the sample kit before Jen sits down.
plays.receipt: Both proof objects open locally; no private client detail is visible in the sample.

plays.title: Capture the permission event
plays.intent: Separate permission to show internal examples from permission to use Jen's name or results publicly.
plays.command: Record Jen's answer in the proof ledger and save the permission receipt in proof/00-permissions/.
plays.receipt: A dated permission record names internal, named, and public-use boundaries separately.

plays.title: Release only the first three asks
plays.intent: Test the ready SKU before investing in the unfinished install.
plays.command: After Jen approves, personalize the three existing DMs. Farrice sends them manually.
plays.receipt: Three dated sends; replies, payments, and collected revenue reported separately.

blocks.label: Jen show-and-ask
blocks.text: I built two connected things I want to show you. First is First Home Valley—the buyer-education and follow-up system for your business. Second is a smaller listing-launch package I could make for a few agents you trust. I want your honest reaction to the first, and your permission before I show any of your listing work to anyone. If you like the agent package, would you be comfortable with me offering three founding spots to people on the team?

blocks.label: Agent with a live listing
blocks.text: Hey [name]—Jen said it was okay for me to show you the listing-launch system I built around her content. I turn one active listing into the shoot plan, three ready-to-read reels, captions, stories, a DM keyword flow, and a fair-housing check. I am opening three founding kits at $200 before the standard price becomes $450. Want to see the sample?

blocks.label: No-active-listing fallback
blocks.text: No active listing is fine. The same founding spot can become an Agent Engine Starter: a profile fix plus ten ready-to-film scripts in your voice and a two-week plan. Same $200 founding rate. Want to see what the output looks like?

sections.heading: what this plan does *not* claim
sections.body:
The Listing Launch Kit has not been sold yet. First Home Valley has not produced a qualified lead or closing yet. A post, view, DM, fit call, deposit, full payment, referral, listing appointment, signed client, and closing are different events and must remain separate.

The $600 target requires three $200 payments, not three expressions of interest. The copy above is prepared only; no message has been sent and no permission has been inferred. Jen's service and her network introduction should remain relationally separate: help her first, then ask.
